sections.title: THE DOG

sections.title: THE CAR
sections.passage:
The sun was just below the distant hills when the car's engine suddenly stopped.

"Why didn't I stop and fill up?" Mum asked.'

She banged her hands on the steering wheel. We both went very quiet.

We got out and pushed the car to the side of the road. Then we looked around. There was nothing but flat, empty land stretching towards the hills. We looked hopefully along the straight road. There wasn't another car in sight. A cold wind was blowing. We were soon back in the car. We could only wait and hope.

When it was dark Mum must have thought I was worried. She suggested a game of I Spy. It wasn't easy to play, so we sang some of our favourite songs.

At last we saw two headlights. We couldn't believe our eyes when we saw what kind of vehicle it was.

The driver winched our car up so that the front wheels were off the ground. We climbed into the cab of the truck and headed for the next town.

responses.prompt: Was Mum upset when the car's engine stopped? How do you know that?
Why did the car's engine stop?
Why did they get back into the car?
Why wasn't it easy to play 'I Spy'?
What sort of vehicle stopped to help them?

questionScores.rationale: 'Monday' is a valid day before Good Friday, matching the guide's accepted example.
Lists a correct time (morning) alongside an incorrect one (afternoon, still hot) with a flippant, no-reasoning tone — matches the guide's explicit reject case.
Gives reasoning ('end of play') but never names a location (school/classroom), which the question requires.
Bare 'no' with no supporting evidence for the 'how do you know' part.
Incorrect and unsupported — the text shows Mum was upset (banging the wheel, self-blame).
'No' does not answer the 'why' question about running out of fuel.
'No' does not answer the 'why' question about sheltering from the cold wind.
'No' does not answer the 'why' question about it being dark.
'No' does not name the tow truck that stopped to help.
